## 固定收益市場主線

民主黨拿下國會兩院，加上油價重挫，緩解了進一步擴張財政及伊朗戰爭推升通膨的疑慮，美國公債因而上漲。10年期殖利率下降7.42個基點至4.8879%，跌幅主要來自通膨補償降低。股市扭轉選舉結果出爐後的初步跌勢，但市場氣氛改善之下，為人工智慧建設籌資的企業表現明顯分歧。

選舉對信用市場最直接的影響，是投資人重新評估擬議中的資料中心限制措施。市場擔憂開發進度延後，CoreWeave債券跌至新低；Meta則因資本支出可能放慢、未來借款需求有望降低，信用保護成本隨之下降。儘管如此，Meta仍在首次歐元債發行籌得€90億，吸引創紀錄的€530億訂單，支付的風險溢酬卻高於其他大型科技發行人。

美國財政部的再融資公告帶來另一項幅度較溫和的調整：官員修改指引，卻未縮減標售規模，促使交易商延後、甚至放棄長債供給將減少的預測。同時，美國服務業調查走弱但仍顯示擴張，ADP就業增幅優於預期，服務業投入價格也居高不下。當天市場對通膨風險要求的補償降低，對聯準會進一步緊縮的預期卻未同步明顯退潮。

## 美債受惠風險緩解，標售規模維持不變

選舉結果逐漸顯示川普總統的立法議程將受到制約，債市漲勢隨之展開。民主黨至少翻轉7席參議院席次，並取得兩院控制權，新一屆國會明年1月就任後，將可主導國會議程。投資人預期，執政黨僅靠本黨票數通過更多減稅或支出的空間縮小。惠靈頓投資管理的Brij Khurana認為，分立政府意味著財政擴張較少；川普則表示將接受結果，並與民主黨合作。

最初的市場反應也包含對成長的疑慮。投資人考量科技與AI投資可能面臨更嚴格監管，股指期貨下跌；依Bloomberg早盤報導，5年期美債殖利率一度下降9個基點至4.67%。隨後股指期貨翻揚，債券吐回部分漲幅。到了當日收盤，油價下跌進一步支持公債需求，股市也同步上漲。

收盤以中天期美債表現最佳。5年期殖利率下降7.64個基點至4.6859%；2年期下降5個基點至4.5809%，30年期下降5.03個基點至5.2762%。2年與10年期利差收窄2.42個基點至30.7個基點，但涵蓋更長區間的2年與30年期利差幾乎不變，為69.53個基點。殖利率曲線並非各段均勻收斂，而是中段表現優於兩端。

通膨因素尤其關鍵。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降5.94個基點至2.2485%，同天期抗通膨公債（TIPS）實質殖利率僅下降1.48個基點至2.6394%。布蘭特原油期貨下跌8.66%至每桶$94.63，西德州原油下跌8.38%至$88.04。布蘭特原油一週累計下跌15.24%，顯示能源成本回落的幅度遠不只是選舉當晚的短暫波動。

較長期間的利率回落仍不均衡。10年期殖利率較一週前低12.96個基點，較一個月前低38.51個基點；30年期一週則僅下降6.64個基點。10年期實質殖利率一週仍上升0.79個基點，通膨補償卻下降13.75個基點。因此，這一週名目殖利率下滑的組成，與一個月來的走勢不同；後者伴隨實質殖利率下降26.96個基點。

財政部未如部分交易商預期，立即減少長天期供給。公告表示，未來幾季名目附息債券與浮動利率債券標售規模維持不變，但刪除了此前「至少」維持這段期間不變的限定。官員保留日後調整的彈性，並未宣布縮減20年或30年期標售。

公告後，長天期債券最初落後短天期，反映供給減量預期落空；之後油價下跌才帶動各天期殖利率普遍走低。花旗原先預估本月起縮減長債標售，如今已不再預期減量。該行策略師Alejandra Vazquez Plata與Jason Williams改為預測，2年至10年期債券發行將於2028年2月增加，最早可能提前至2027年底。

道明證券與富國銀行則將短天期債券增額、長債減額的預測時點，由明年初延至2027年8月。巴克萊同樣預期8月調整，但僅有中短天期債券增額，長債規模不變。公告主要改變的是交易商預期的調整時點與發行組合，而非當下供給量。

美國財政部借款諮詢委員會（TBAC）表示，委員普遍同意額外發行應集中於2年至10年期。討論20年與30年期供給可能調整時，委員會強調溝通必須清楚，並維持規律、可預測的操作架構。財政部助理部長Hunter McMaster重申，融資決策將以長期成本最低為依歸。

債券買回仍維持相當規模，但未宣布進一步擴大。接下來的較長天期買回操作，最高購買額為$60億，與8月提高上限後的近期做法一致。財政部將持續評估購買上限、時程、頻率、合資格證券及操作方式。買回處理的是已流通債券，與新債標售規模維持不變是兩回事。

融資上的取捨並未消失。TBAC指出，貨幣市場基金資產已趨於持平，國庫券開始顯現價格敏感性。財政部顧問與市場人士提及，確定給付制退休基金對長天期資產的需求減弱；但若更依賴國庫券，債務利息支出就會對短期利率更加敏感。穩定幣帶動的國庫券需求，也尚未達到官員所談論的規模。

選舉同樣沒有解決既有財政收支問題。瑞萬通博的Andrew Jackson區分了阻止進一步擴張，與縮減既有赤字這兩件事。關於兩黨可能達成協議的新報導顯示，增加國內支出及追加國防撥款的壓力仍在。目前債務上限為$41.1兆，尚餘約$8,000億空間；策略師預期2027年上半年將觸及上限，之後再以非常措施延長融資能力。目前國庫券曲線未顯示明顯疑慮，但圍繞最終現金耗盡期限的談判，走勢可能與週三這波風險緩解行情截然不同。

## 服務業放緩，通膨問題仍未解

當天美國數據描繪的是持續擴張但力道減弱，而非經濟活動全面轉差。10月ADP民間就業增加8.6萬人，高於市場預期的6.9萬人，與上月修正後的8.6萬人相同。招聘優於預期，但相較修正後的前月基準並未加速。

服務業調查較弱。標普全球服務業PMI終值由58.8降至56.1，低於預期的57.9；綜合PMI由58.4降至55.9，也低於預期的57.6。兩者仍高於50榮枯分界，但降幅顯示該調查衡量的擴張力道減弱。

另一項ISM服務業PMI由54.9小降至54.5，略低於路透調查預期的54.8，10月仍是服務業連續第28個月擴張。不過，細項中的活動與訂單成長放緩較明顯：商業活動指數由56.5降至53.8，新訂單由59.8降至55.9。

就業則反向改善。ISM就業指數由50.1升至51.4，連續第二個月高於50，反映受訪服務業企業的招聘擴張更為普遍，同時訂單仍在減速。這是招聘情況的擴散指標，並非新增就業人數，也使聯準會更有理由區分需求降溫與勞動市場已陷入萎縮。

供給情況讓判斷更加複雜。供應商交貨指數由53.2升至56.7，代表交貨放慢；價格指數則僅由74.0降至73.0，過去八個月已有七個月高於70，並連續23個月高於60。價格指數的12個月平均升至69.2，為2023年4月以來最高。價格降幅小於活動及訂單，顯示成長轉弱之際，成本壓力仍相當大。

這也有助解釋，名目殖利率下降為何不必然伴隨近期政策預期等幅轉變。Bloomberg週三利率報導指出，交換市場隱含聯準會12月升息機率約85%，當天變化不大，2027年至少再升息一次的預期也維持穩定。選舉與油價走勢降低了長債定價中的部分風險，但新出爐經濟數據仍支持維持政策緊縮。

房市更明顯反映緊縮效果。美國抵押貸款銀行協會（MBA）公布，截至10月30日當週，30年期契約房貸利率下降7個基點至7.30%，連續第三週下降，卻仍比一年前高近1個百分點。購屋貸款申請減少2%，過去九週已有八週下降，接近2025年1月以來最低。整體房貸申請在前週增加3.4%後減少1.2%，轉貸申請僅略增。借款利率連續數週回落，仍未帶動購屋需求持續復甦。

貿易方面，單月收支略有改善，近期移動平均卻較不利。9月商品與服務貿易逆差由修正後的$1,057億收窄至$1,050億，優於預期的$1,080億。出口增加1.9%至$3,215億，進口增加1.2%至$4,266億；商品逆差收窄至$1,359億，服務貿易順差則小降至$309億。

但截至9月的三個月平均逆差擴大$113億至$1,012億，平均進口增加$127億至$4,172億，遠高於出口增加的$14億，後者達$3,160億。今年累計逆差仍較2025年同期少12.2%。這些名目、經季節調整數據涵蓋不同期間：9月改善與近期三個月平均惡化同時存在，尚非持續的單月改善趨勢。

參議院選舉結果也改變了貨幣政策的制度環境。Elizabeth Warren可能出任銀行委員會主席，讓民主黨有機會阻擋被認為過度迎合白宮壓力的聯準會提名人。目前七人組成的理事會沒有空缺，Jerome Powell的理事任期到2028年1月。PGIM的Daleep Singh認為，選舉可能讓央行更能自主對抗通膨。

這項保障主要在於人事任命，並不意味行政部門不再施壓。美國企業研究所經濟學家Michael Strain表示，對現任官員的威脅，以及可能動用刑事調查，仍是更重要的風險。市場一方面預期繼續緊縮，另一方面也預期參議院將更積極維護聯準會自主性；央行本身並未宣布改變政策取向。

## 資料中心限制措施牽動信用市場分化

放慢資料中心建設的提議，在AI融資鏈不同環節引發相反反應。德州州長當選人Gina Hinojosa主張立即暫停開發，俄亥俄州與喬治亞州勝選的民主黨候選人也以減緩建設為競選訴求。Bloomberg報導指出，德州約13吉瓦規劃中容量面臨延後或遷址風險；州長選舉結果可能使全美規劃新增容量約一半，受到更嚴格的地方審查。

對仰賴專案完工帶來收入的開發商而言，延誤會威脅原先舉債所依據的進度安排。依Trace資料，CoreWeave的2031年到期無擔保債券最低跌至面額的79.5%，成為週三表現最弱的高收益債之一。2030年及2032年到期債券也下跌，殖利率超過15%；股價下跌9.9%至$48.42，創2025年5月以來收盤新低。

CoreWeave對政治變化將影響已簽約業務的看法提出異議。發言人表示，目前不預期政治變動會影響既有客戶承諾及相關未履行訂單，並認為已投入運作的容量將格外有價值。投資人重新評估開發與融資風險之際，公司仍維持既有承諾的展望。

Galaxy Digital與Stingray Compute債券也走弱。花旗高收益債策略師Steph Choe指出，專案所處階段很重要：已取得電力供應與許可的設施，比仍待環評或核准的專案更難被新政府叫停。花旗研究顯示，2026年發行的資料中心債券10月下跌3.2%，2025年發行者則下跌1.5%。這組比較發生在市場回應選舉之前，但呈現了較新開發風險與進度較成熟專案的差異。

大型科技客戶可能面臨的現金流效果不同。駿利亨德森的Bradford Smith表示，擴張放慢可能降低近期資本支出與發債需求，讓既有合約有更多時間發展成熟、產生回報。依ICE Data Services，Meta的5年期信用違約交換（CDS）成本下降8.7個基點至約110個基點，反映市場重新評估借款需求後，對其信用風險的看法改善。

但Meta已完成的歐元交易也顯示，大額融資需求依然存在。首次歐元債發行籌得€90億，分為六檔，期限從略逾4年到超過38年。認購訂單達€530億，超越Anheuser-Busch InBev於2016年創下逾€310億的歐洲企業債紀錄。

投資人取得的補償相當可觀。Meta支付的風險溢酬，約為Alphabet本週稍早可比較歐元債的1.4倍；6.26年期債券以高於交換利率中間價135個基點定價，Alphabet的6年期則為90個基點，長端差距更大。Bloomberg並報導，Meta短至中天期歐元債支付的溢酬，較其美元債約高15至20個基點，最長天期差距則接近100個基點。

強勁訂單讓整筆交易在定價水準已確定後，仍罕見地再收窄5個基點，但利差依然高於其他超大規模雲端業者的歐元債。Allspring的Alex Temple認為，以評等而言，這些水準具吸引力，但仍擔心明年的融資需求。花旗與摩根士丹利安排本次發行。當天新增的籌資事件是這筆歐元融資，而非週二已完成的美元債發行。

銀行貸款也為基礎設施開發商提供另一條融資管道。橡樹資本支持的Pure Data Centres取得$7.8億融資，另有擴增$11億的選項。花旗、阿布達比第一銀行與Infranity加入荷蘭銀行、安聯及三井住友銀行，共同提供融資。代理執行長Gary Wojtaszek表示，資金將用於一般企業用途，以及歐洲、中東專案的土地購置與能源供應。

Wojtaszek表示，這筆融資使Pure DC過去一年籌資總額超過$60億。公司以3吉瓦容量為目標，近期宣布在芬蘭打造其規模最大的AI園區，客戶包括微軟。今年稍早，公司因傳統貸款機構條件更有利，放棄在北歐債券市場籌資。本次方案包含已籌得的$7.8億及額外擴增額度，而非已動用$19億。

整體市場明顯強於這些與開發相關的債券。美國高收益債利差明顯收窄，標普500上漲1.58%至7,688.62，那斯達克100上漲0.91%，VIX下跌20.26%至16.61。半導體類股卻下跌3.13%，凸顯科技業內部分化。計入配息，LQD與HYG報酬率分別約0.75%與0.70%，EMB為1.01%。美元指數下跌0.36%至101.508，黃金期貨上漲3.34%至每盎司$4,072.20。

在香港國際金融領袖投資峰會上，Davidson Kempner的Tony Yoseloff指出，利率較高、企業成長放緩，以及2027至2028年到期債務，正成為私募信貸日益增加的風險。他表示，美國私募信貸貸款約有三分之一，跟隨私募股權資金流入軟體業。Sona的John Aylward另指出，較廣泛的聯貸市場五年累計違約率，已超過金融危機期間的水準。他比較的是這項聯貸市場累計指標，並關注兩個市場重疊的私募股權支持借款人，以及規模較小的私募信貸企業，而非表示兩個市場已出現相同的違約率。

## 通膨使全球政策步調持續分歧

儘管新數據顯示通膨持續，歐洲債券仍跟隨上漲。Bloomberg市場報導指出，德國10年期殖利率下降6個基點至3.27%，英國下降13個基點至5.13%。歐盟統計局公布，歐元區10月通膨由3.8%升至4%，為2023年9月以來最高，符合經濟學家預期；核心通膨維持2.5%，服務通膨小升至3.3%。

歐洲央行薪資追蹤指標則提供較有利的前瞻訊息，預估2027年第1、2季薪資年增率均為2.8%，第3季放慢至2.4%。這些已議定薪資的訊號顯示，未來薪資壓力可能減輕，即使當前能源成本正推高整體通膨。Bloomberg Economics的David Powell認為，對基礎通膨的傳導仍有限，預期12月最後一次升息後，本輪升息循環便告結束。

荷蘭週三確認提名Klaas Knot角逐歐洲央行總裁，他強調的則是另一面風險。Knot預期，商品與服務的第二輪效應將推高核心通膨，主張面對接連發生的供給衝擊，應採取略偏鷹派立場。他是前荷蘭央行總裁，並非現任國家央行總裁；他強調政策落後時間很長，現在設定的利率，約18個月至兩年後才會發揮效果。其警告著眼於未來成本傳導，薪資追蹤指標則顯示協議薪資成長將放緩。

瑞典立即採取行動。瑞典央行一致決議將政策利率由1.75%調升至2%，為2023年以來首次升息，並表示若通膨與經濟活動展望維持，明年可能進一步緊縮。本次非預測更新會議未公布新預測或利率路徑。總裁Erik Thedéen表示，既有路徑隱含未來一年升息次數略少於兩次，但未承諾特定會議採取行動。

Nordea解讀這項指引為12月升息可能性不高，預期下次行動在2月。野村預估2月與5月各升息25個基點，但兩次都可能各延後一個月。Bloomberg Economics預測2027年初再升息一次至2.25%，風險偏向進一步緊縮。瑞典較強勁的成長也是判斷依據之一：儘管水力、核能發電與燃料稅減免緩和能源衝擊，財政部近期仍將2026年成長預估調升至3%。

波蘭則連續第八個月維持利率3.75%，同時大幅上修2027年通膨預測，區間由7月的1.5%至4%調至3.1%至5.3%。政府恢復燃料價格上限後，10月通膨由4.1%降至3.5%。Bank Pekao經濟學家表示，貨幣政策委員會希望觀察價格上限是否延長，以及第二輪壓力是否出現在實際數據中。

波蘭2年期本幣債殖利率下降11個基點至4.83%，茲羅提兌歐元升值0.4%。ING的Rafal Benecki仍預期2027年第1季累計升息50個基點，但表示若能源價格持續下降，升息需求就會減弱。另方面，總理圖斯克批准央行管理委員會人事任命，結束一場營運爭議，卻未解決國會尋求將總裁Adam Glapinski移送審判的行動。Glapinski否認相關不當行為指控；人事任命與可能停職分屬不同的制度決策。

英國最新服務業調查與研究，為市場預期的英格蘭銀行升息提供了更強的需求背景。標普全球服務業PMI由52.1升至52.8，為2月以來最強。新訂單回升，員工人數在長期縮減後增加，投入價格通膨升至五個月高點。IT與專業服務受惠於AI相關企業投資，但面向消費者的企業仍反映需求較弱。

Bloomberg Economics的Simon Lloyd與Dan Hanson質疑英格蘭銀行認為政策已具緊縮性的評估。他們估算的超額需求自2023年第4季以來一直在狹窄區間內波動，2026年第2季為潛在產出的負0.2%。兩人認為，經濟比央行假設的更接近不引發通膨的產能水準，利率對支出大致呈中性，並預測本週四與2月將升息。這是對經濟狀態的另一種研究估算，而非央行官方重估。

澳洲9月家庭支出也顯示需求韌性，但價格與數量走勢有別。支出繼前月下降0.1%後，月增0.6%，高於預期的0.2%；年增6.8%，達約A$826億。必要性支出增加1.2%，各州與領地名目支出均上升。燃料支出跳增5.4%，部分反映油價較高及燃料稅減免結束，但實驗性統計的燃料用量下降2.2%。全季實質家庭支出增加0.7%，連續第四季成長。

中國RatingDog服務業PMI由51.6降至50.8，低於預期的51.7，為7月以來最低。出口訂單連續第六個月擴張，招聘也持續增加，但售價連續第二個月下降，投入成本卻以五個月來最快速度上升。調查反映的是利潤率與信心承壓，而非英國所呈現的國內定價力較強。

巴西央行一致決議維持Selic利率13.75%，結束連續五次降息，符合受訪31位經濟學家中26位的預期。聲明同時提及通膨預期上升、不確定性增加，以及經濟放緩更為明顯。決策安排在巴西利亞時間晚間6時30分之後，已接近美國交易日尾聲，是獨立的政策發展，而非稍早美債上漲的原因。在本週稍早已報導選舉帶動未來利率預期重估之後，這次新增訊息是暫停降息本身及決策委員會的評估。

智利新公布的10月27日會議紀錄顯示，決策者最後維持利率4.5%之前，曾認真考慮升息25個基點。部分委員認為，面對更大的成本衝擊，有充分理由緊縮；其他委員則強調需求可能持續疲弱。紀錄揭示的是委員會內確實存在的政策選項，並未宣布新一輪升息。

## 舉債授權與債權人權利的新進展

初步計票顯示，美國選民批准至少$670億州及地方政府發債授權，形成未來融資案源，而非立即發行。其中加州兩大提案分別為$250億購屋協助收益債，以及$112.5億可負擔住宅一般責任債；密西根州Dearborn公立學區則獲准籌措$15億進行建築工程。

全美提出的授權案至少$840億，高於2024年討論的約$810億，但並非所有借款人都獲授權。德州選民否決Cypress-Fairbanks學區$16億及Irving學區$9.52億的方案。富蘭克林坦伯頓的Jennifer Johnston認為，部分提案遭否決與民眾抗拒增稅有關，即使人口增加正推升基礎設施需求。選舉擴大了未來舉債規模，部分快速成長社區卻未獲得原擬的融資授權。

企業信用市場則面臨不同的投資人權利爭議。Electronic Arts（EA）週二起訴債券受託人US Bank，要求法院確認其槓桿收購後並未違約。聲稱持有超過$14億債券的債權人指控，公司未依規定支付控制權變更款項。EA則主張，Egan-Jones給予的投資級評等，使其得以採取債務清償安排（defeasance），以美國公債擔保未來付款，從而免除該項支付義務。

爭議涉及的金額不小。EA於2月提出的收購要約，對2031年到期、票息1.85%的債券，每面額1美元支付約92美分；對2051年到期、票息2.95%的債券，則約74美分，低於通常控制權變更支付的101美分。Bloomberg先前估算，若策略成功，EA約可節省$2.5億。EA如今表示，債權人採取救濟措施可能觸發約$180億母公司債務的交叉違約條款。這是公司對爭議潛在後果的主張，其是否違約仍待法院判定。

收購融資也持續準備進入市場。摩根大通與美國銀行正為CVC收購IFF食品原料事業，準備向潛在投資人初步推介約$24億跨境貸款。摩根大通主導歐元部分，美國銀行負責美元部分，後者可能約$15億，預計未來數週展開更廣泛的聯貸募集。該收購對事業的估值為$43億，IFF保留10%權益；貸款目前仍處於擬議分銷階段。

印度新報導的家庭債務比較，揭示消費成長背後的制約。央行數據顯示，截至3月的一年，家庭借款成長36%，消費者債務達GDP的46%，創歷史新高。Centre for Social and Economic Progress數據顯示，2025至2026年借款成長速度約為可支配所得的四倍。里昂證券估計，截至2025年3月的一年，償債支出約占家庭所得13%，高於此前十年大部分時間的10%至11%。

報導指出，廣泛還款壓力的證據仍有限，銀行不良貸款比率接近數十年低點。不過，Bajaj Finance與Piramal Finance發現，部分陷入困境的借款人，利用黃金抵押貸款支應其在其他機構已違約的授信。這項觀察僅針對這些借款人，並非所有印度消費者。截至3月的一年，黃金抵押借款增加近45%，貸款機構也將個人信貸轉向較高所得借款人。財政部長Nirmala Sitharaman則強調消費具有持續性，借款速度與償債負擔因而成為雙方分歧的核心。

肯亞則獲得一項有條件的評估，說明治理改善可能如何有利主權融資。世界銀行新模型估計，相較不改革情境，溫和反貪腐改革可使2035年GDP提高8.7%，力度較強的措施則可提高22.3%。模型估計，債務占GDP比率相較維持現狀最多可降低18%，並非已減少18個百分點。世銀表示，若肯亞的貪腐觀感評分能追上象牙海岸、迦納或塞內加爾，外部借款成本可能降低50至100個基點，每年節省$5,000萬至$1億。

肯亞也正尋求$10億債務交換以支持糧食計畫。擬以再融資節省款項支持這類用途，顯示部分開發中國家的債務轉換，正由保育轉向眼前的生活負擔與教育需求。Nuveen的Stephen Liberatore預期，明年將有數筆公開發行的債務轉換交易。另方面，世界銀行的Paschal Donohoe主張撒哈拉以南非洲增加市政發債，但前提是城市具備償還自身債務所需的領導能力與課稅能力。這些是潛在融資管道，尚非已完成的債務減輕，也未宣布新一波城市發債。

## 後續市場焦點

美國週四將於美東時間上午8時30分公布初領失業救濟金與第3季生產力。初領人數預期由19.4萬增至19.6萬，生產力增幅預期由1.4%升至2.5%。在週三民間招聘優於預期、服務業訂單放慢及投入成本持續偏高之後，這些數據將補充裁員與產出效率的資訊。Beth Hammack與Tom Barkin安排週四發言，Lorie Logan則於當晚發言，可供觀察官員如何評估本週數據與能源價格重估對政策的影響。

週五10月就業報告仍是更重要的勞動市場事件。市場預期非農就業增加6.5萬人，高於前月的2.9萬人，整體U-3失業率維持4.2%；平均時薪預期月增0.3%、年增2.9%。在市場仍認為12月升息機率很高之際，就業與薪資的組合將格外重要。接著公布的11月密西根大學消費者信心指數初值，市場預期為48；John Williams、Alberto Musalem與Michelle Bowman也都安排週五公開露面。

英格蘭銀行週四決策將顯示，官員如何看待企業服務較強、面向家庭需求較弱的分歧。市場普遍預期升息25個基點至4%，真正的不確定性在於官員認為還需緊縮多少，尤其Bloomberg Economics質疑現行利率已壓抑支出的假設。荷蘭確認提名Knot後，歐洲央行總裁提名將於週五截止，財長們11月9日將檢視提名情況，但目前未預期屆時作出決定。

美國財政部將於11月9日標售$580億3年期債券、11月10日標售$420億10年期債券，以及11月12日標售$250億30年期債券。這輪總額$1,250億的再融資已連續第11次維持不變。公告未改變標售規模，卻使交易商把預測調整時點推得更遠，接下來將觀察實際認購需求。債務上限談判則是另一項更長期風險：觸及法定上限，與採用非常措施後現金耗盡，分屬不同階段；特定到期日國庫券是否受擾動，將取決於最終融資期限。

AI信用市場待觀察的是，新任州長如何將競選承諾化為許可決策，以及如何處理既有核准與客戶合約。CoreWeave表示不預期既有承諾受到影響，市場則擔憂開發延誤，兩者將接受個別專案決策的考驗，而非由單一全國規則決定。Meta創紀錄的歐元訂單，也讓後續融資成本持續受到關注：取得資金的能力依然強勁，但付出的價格與同業明顯不同。

能源外交仍有獨立重要性。川普表示，美國目前沒有立即升高伊朗衝突的計畫；法國財政部長Roland Lescure則提醒，即使選舉結果改變，外交權限仍掌握在總統手中。伊朗與美國正檢視調停方提案，但對回應內容仍有分歧。這個過程能否延續原油跌勢，將影響週三通膨補償下降能維持多久；選舉結果本身既未解決談判，也未恢復不受限制的能源運輸。

overall_summary.headline: 民主黨掌控國會、油價重挫緩解財政與通膨風險，美債上漲
overall_summary.session_narrative:
民主黨拿下國會兩院，限制進一步財政擴張的空間，加上油價大跌緩解通膨風險，美國公債上漲。10年期殖利率下降7.42個基點至4.8879%，其中通膨補償下降5.94個基點至2.2485%，實質殖利率下降1.48個基點至2.6394%。中天期表現最佳，2年與10年期利差收窄2.42個基點至30.7個基點；布蘭特原油下跌8.66%至每桶$94.63。

財政部修改指引，但維持標售規模不變，促使交易商延後、甚至放棄長債供給減量的預測。服務業調查雖走弱，仍顯示擴張，ADP招聘優於預期，服務業投入成本也持續偏高。市場對聯準會12月緊縮的預期幾乎未變。

擬議中的資料中心限制措施使信用市場分化。開發延誤疑慮令CoreWeave債券跌至新低，但公司表示，不預期既有承諾受到影響。Meta則因投資人預期未來借款減少，信用保護成本下降；不過，其首次歐元債發行仍籌得€90億，訂單創紀錄達€530億，支付的溢酬高於同業。股市回升之際，美國整體高收益債利差明顯收窄。能源外交能否延續原油低價，仍攸關這波由通膨因素帶動的債市漲勢。
overall_summary.summary: 美債漲勢主要來自通膨補償下降，市場對聯準會12月緊縮的預期卻幾乎未變；擬議中的資料中心限制措施衝擊開發商，但使Meta的未來借款需求展望趨緩。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied as Democrats won both chambers of Congress and oil prices plunged, bringing relief from the prospect of further fiscal expansion and the inflationary cost of the Iran war. The 10-year yield fell 7.42 basis points to 4.8879%, with lower inflation compensation accounting for most of the decline. Stocks recovered from an initially adverse election response, but the improvement in sentiment concealed a sharp division among companies financing the artificial-intelligence buildout.

The election's most immediate credit consequence was a reassessment of proposed data-center restrictions. CoreWeave bonds fell to new lows as investors weighed delays to development, while Meta's credit protection became cheaper on expectations that slower capital spending could reduce future borrowing. Meta nevertheless raised €9 billion in its first euro bond sale, drawing a record €53 billion of orders while paying more than other large technology issuers.

Treasury's refunding announcement supplied a separate, more measured adjustment. Officials changed their guidance without cutting auction sizes, prompting dealers to push back or abandon forecasts for reductions in long-bond supply. Meanwhile, U.S. services surveys softened but continued to show expansion, ADP hiring exceeded expectations, and service-sector input prices remained elevated. The session lowered the market price of inflation risk without producing a comparable retreat in expectations for Federal Reserve tightening.

## Treasury Relief Meets Unchanged Auction Sizes

The bond rally began as election results pointed to constraints on President Donald Trump's legislative agenda. Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats and secured control of both houses, giving them authority over the congressional agenda when the new Congress takes office in January. Investors anticipated less scope for additional tax cuts or spending enacted on party-line votes. Wellington Management's Brij Khurana associated divided government with less fiscal expansion, while Trump said he would accept the results and work with Democrats.

The first reaction also contained concern about growth. Equity futures fell as investors considered tighter oversight of technology and AI investment, and the five-year Treasury yield declined as much as 9 basis points to 4.67% in Bloomberg's early trading account. Bonds subsequently surrendered part of that advance as stock futures reversed higher. By the completed session, cheaper oil had reinforced the demand for government debt even as equities rallied.

Intermediate maturities led the closing advance. The five-year yield fell 7.64 basis points to 4.6859%, compared with a 5-basis-point decline in the two-year to 4.5809% and a 5.03-basis-point fall in the 30-year to 5.2762%. The two- to 10-year gap narrowed 2.42 basis points to 30.7 basis points. Across the longer two- to 30-year span, the spread was almost unchanged at 69.53 basis points. This was not a uniform compression of every part of the curve: the middle outperformed both ends.

The inflation component was particularly important. The 10-year breakeven fell 5.94 basis points to 2.2485%, while the corresponding TIPS real yield declined only 1.48 basis points to 2.6394%. Brent futures dropped 8.66% to $94.63 a barrel and WTI fell 8.38% to $88.04. Over the week, Brent was down 15.24%, giving the retreat in energy costs considerably more substance than a single election-night fluctuation.

The broader rates recovery remained uneven. Ten-year yields were 12.96 basis points below their week-earlier level and 38.51 basis points lower over the month. The 30-year's weekly decline was only 6.64 basis points. At 10 years, real yields were still 0.79 basis point higher over the week, against a 13.75-basis-point decline in inflation compensation. The weekly nominal rally therefore depended on a different balance from the month-long recovery, during which real yields had fallen 26.96 basis points.

Treasury's announcement did not deliver the immediate long-end supply reduction some dealers had expected. It said nominal coupon and floating-rate-note auction sizes would remain unchanged for the next several quarters, removing the previous qualification that they would stay unchanged for at least that period. Officials retained flexibility over future changes but made no announcement of smaller 20- or 30-year auctions.

The initial curve reaction reflected that disappointment: longer maturities underperformed shorter ones after the statement, before the oil decline helped pull yields lower across the market. Citi, which had anticipated cuts to long-bond auctions beginning this month, now expects no reductions. Its strategists Alejandra Vazquez Plata and Jason Williams instead envisage increases in two- to 10-year note sales in February 2028, potentially as early as late 2027.

TD Securities and Wells Fargo delayed their forecasts for both larger shorter-note auctions and smaller long-bond auctions to August 2027 from early next year. Barclays also expects changes in August, but only increases in notes, leaving long-bond sizes unchanged. Those revisions illustrate the announcement's principal effect: it changed the timing and composition dealers expect, rather than the amount of debt immediately being offered.

The Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee said members generally agreed that additional issuance should be concentrated in the two- to 10-year sector. Its discussion of possible changes to 20- and 30-year supply came with an emphasis on clear communication and a regular, predictable operating framework. Treasury Assistant Secretary Hunter McMaster reiterated that financing decisions would be guided by the lowest cost over time.

Buybacks also remained substantial without a newly announced expansion. Upcoming longer-dated operations will have maximum purchases of $6 billion, consistent with recent practice following August's increase. Treasury said it would continue evaluating purchase limits, scheduling, frequency, eligible securities and execution. These purchases address outstanding securities, separately from the unchanged sizes of new auctions.

The financing trade-off has not disappeared. TBAC noted that money-market fund assets had leveled off and bills were beginning to show price sensitivity. Treasury's advisers and market participants have pointed to weaker demand for long-dated assets from defined-benefit pension funds, but greater reliance on bills increases the sensitivity of debt-service costs to short-term rates. Stablecoin-related bill demand has yet to emerge at the scale officials have discussed.

Nor did the election settle the fiscal arithmetic. Vontobel's Andrew Jackson distinguished preventing new expansion from reducing an existing deficit. Fresh reporting on possible bipartisan deals identified pressure for both higher domestic spending and additional defense appropriations. The debt limit stands at $41.1 trillion, with about $800 billion of remaining room; strategists expect it to become binding in the first half of 2027, before extraordinary measures extend financing capacity. The bill curve currently shows little concern, but negotiations over the eventual cash deadline could follow a very different course from Wednesday's relief rally.

## Services Slow Without Resolving the Inflation Problem

The day's U.S. releases described continued expansion at a less vigorous pace, rather than a broad break in activity. October ADP private employment rose 86,000, above the 69,000 consensus and matching a revised 86,000 increase in the previous month. That combination supplied a stronger hiring result than expected without showing an acceleration from the revised baseline.

The services surveys were softer. Final S&P Global Services PMI fell to 56.1 from 58.8, below the 57.9 consensus. The composite index declined to 55.9 from 58.4, against expectations of 57.6. Both remained above the 50 threshold, but their declines reduced the strength of the expansion measured by that survey.

ISM's separate headline Services PMI slipped to 54.5 from 54.9, modestly below the Reuters-survey expectation of 54.8. October was the sector's 28th consecutive month of expansion. Beneath the headline, however, activity and order growth slowed more noticeably: Business Activity fell to 53.8 from 56.5 and New Orders to 55.9 from 59.8.

Employment moved in the opposite direction. ISM's employment index rose to 51.4 from 50.1, staying above 50 for a second month. That was a broader hiring signal within the surveyed services businesses, alongside the deceleration in orders, rather than a numerical measure of payroll creation. It gave the Fed another reason to distinguish moderating demand from an already contracting labor market.

Supply performance complicated the picture. Supplier Deliveries rose to 56.7 from 53.2, indicating slower deliveries, while the Prices index eased only to 73.0 from 74.0. Prices remained above 70 for the seventh time in eight months and above 60 for 23 consecutive months. The index's 12-month average reached 69.2, the highest since April 2023. The smaller decline in prices than in activity and orders left substantial cost pressure alongside softer growth.

That combination helps explain why falling nominal yields did not require an equivalent change in the near-term policy outlook. Bloomberg's Wednesday rates account put the swap-implied probability of a December Fed increase around 85%, little changed on the day, with expectations for at least one further increase in 2027 also steady. The election and oil moves reduced some risks priced into longer bonds while the incoming economic observations still supported continued policy restraint.

Housing showed that restraint operating more visibly. The Mortgage Bankers Association's 30-year contract mortgage rate fell 7 basis points to 7.30% in the week ended October 30, its third consecutive weekly decline. It nevertheless remained nearly a percentage point above the year-earlier level. Purchase applications fell 2%, declining in eight of nine weeks and approaching their lowest level since January 2025. Overall mortgage applications fell 1.2% after rising 3.4%, while refinancing barely increased. Lower borrowing rates over several weeks had not produced a sustained recovery in purchases.

Trade supplied a modestly better monthly balance but a less favorable rolling comparison. The September goods-and-services deficit narrowed to $105.0 billion from a revised $105.7 billion, better than the $108 billion consensus. Exports increased 1.9% to $321.5 billion and imports rose 1.2% to $426.6 billion. The goods deficit narrowed to $135.9 billion, while the services surplus edged down to $30.9 billion.

Over the three months ending September, the average deficit instead widened $11.3 billion to $101.2 billion. Average imports rose $12.7 billion to $417.2 billion, far more than the $1.4 billion increase in exports to $316.0 billion. The year-to-date deficit remained 12.2% smaller than in the comparable 2025 period. These nominal, seasonally adjusted measures described distinct horizons: the September improvement coexisted with a recent rolling deterioration, rather than establishing a sustained monthly trend.

The Senate result also changed the institutional setting for monetary policy. Elizabeth Warren is likely to chair the Banking Committee, giving Democrats an opportunity to block Fed nominees considered overly responsive to White House pressure. There are currently no vacancies on the seven-member Board of Governors, and Jerome Powell's governor term runs to January 2028. PGIM's Daleep Singh argued the election could give the central bank greater freedom to fight inflation.

That protection concerns appointments, not an end to executive pressure. American Enterprise Institute economist Michael Strain said threats against sitting officials and the possible use of criminal investigations remained more important risks. The market's expectation of further tightening therefore stood alongside a stronger prospective Senate defense of Fed autonomy, not a newly announced change in the central bank's policy preference.

## Data-Center Restrictions Divide Credit Markets

The proposed slowdown in data-center construction produced opposite reactions across the AI financing chain. Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has called for an immediate development moratorium, and successful Democratic candidates in Ohio and Georgia also campaigned on slowing construction. Bloomberg's reporting put roughly 13 gigawatts of planned Texas capacity at risk of delay or relocation, with half of proposed U.S. additions potentially exposed to stricter local scrutiny following the gubernatorial results.

For developers whose revenues depend on completing those projects, delay threatens the schedule against which debt was raised. CoreWeave's unsecured 2031 bonds traded as low as 79.5 cents on the dollar, according to Trace, making them among Wednesday's weakest high-yield securities. Its 2030 and 2032 obligations also declined, with yields above 15%. The company's shares fell 9.9% to $48.42, their lowest close since May 2025.

CoreWeave disputed the implication for its contracted business. A spokesperson said the company did not currently expect political changes to affect existing customer commitments or the associated backlog, and expected active capacity to be especially valuable. Investors were thus repricing development and financing risk while the issuer maintained its outlook for commitments already in place.

Galaxy Digital and Stingray Compute debt also weakened. Citi high-yield strategist Steph Choe said the construction stage matters: facilities with power secured and permits already in place are harder for a new administration to stop than projects still requiring environmental review or approvals. Citi research put October declines in data-center bonds issued during 2026 at 3.2%, compared with 1.5% for those issued in 2025. That comparison preceded the election response but identifies a distinction between newer development exposure and more advanced projects.

The large technology customers faced a different prospective cash-flow effect. Slower expansion could reduce near-term capital spending and issuance, allowing more time for existing contracts to mature and returns to develop, Janus Henderson's Bradford Smith said. Meta's five-year credit-default-swap cost fell 8.7 basis points to about 110 basis points, according to ICE Data Services. This was an improvement in the market's assessment of its credit risk as borrowing expectations were reconsidered.

Meta's completed euro transaction demonstrated that large funding needs continued alongside that reassessment. The €9 billion debut was split into six parts, with maturities ranging from just over four years to more than 38 years. Orders reached €53 billion, exceeding the previous European corporate record of more than €31 billion for Anheuser-Busch InBev in 2016.

Investors received substantial compensation. Meta paid roughly 1.4 times the risk premium Alphabet offered on comparable euro bonds earlier in the week. Its 6.26-year tranche priced at 135 basis points over mid-swaps, compared with 90 basis points for Alphabet's six-year issue. The difference was greater at the long end. Bloomberg reported that Meta also paid around 15-20 basis points more than in its dollar offering at short-to-intermediate maturities, and closer to 100 basis points more at the longest end.

The order book enabled an unusual extra tightening of 5 basis points across the deal after pricing levels had previously been set, yet spreads remained wider than those of other hyperscaler euro offerings. Allspring's Alex Temple described the levels as attractive for the rating while retaining concern about next year's funding requirements. Citi and Morgan Stanley arranged the sale. The new euro financing, rather than Tuesday's already completed dollar sale, was the day's additional capital-raising event.

Bank lending supplied another route for infrastructure developers. Oaktree-backed Pure Data Centres raised $780 million with an option to expand the financing by $1.1 billion. Citi, First Abu Dhabi Bank and Infranity joined ABN Amro, Allianz and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. in supplying the package. Interim Chief Executive Gary Wojtaszek said proceeds would support general corporate purposes, land purchases and energy supplies for projects across Europe and the Middle East.

Pure DC's financing raised its total capital raised over the past year above $6 billion, according to Wojtaszek. The developer targets 3 gigawatts of capacity and recently announced its largest AI campus in Finland, with Microsoft among its customers. Earlier this year it abandoned a Nordic bond-market financing effort after finding traditional lenders offered more favorable terms. The current package comprises the $780 million raised and additional expansion capacity, rather than $1.9 billion already drawn.

Broad markets were considerably firmer than these development-linked credits. U.S. high-yield spreads tightened clearly. The S&P 500 gained 1.58% to 7,688.62, the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.91% and the VIX fell 20.26% to 16.61. Semiconductor shares nevertheless lost 3.13%, underscoring the dispersion within technology. LQD and HYG returned approximately 0.75% and 0.70%, respectively, including distributions, while EMB returned 1.01%. The Dollar Index fell 0.36% to 101.508 and gold futures rose 3.34% to $4,072.20 an ounce.

At Hong Kong's Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit, Davidson Kempner's Tony Yoseloff identified higher rates, slower business growth and maturities in 2027-2028 as growing risks for private credit. He said roughly a third of U.S. private-credit loans had followed private-equity capital into software. Sona's John Aylward separately said the broader syndicated-loan market's five-year cumulative default rate had exceeded levels seen during the financial crisis. His comparison concerned that cumulative loan-market measure, alongside concern about overlapping sponsor borrowers and smaller private-credit companies, rather than an observed common default rate across both markets.

## Inflation Keeps Global Policy Paths Uneven

European bonds participated in the rally despite fresh evidence of inflation persistence. Bloomberg's market account put Germany's 10-year yield down 6 basis points at 3.27% and Britain's down 13 basis points at 5.13%. Eurostat reported October euro-area inflation at 4%, up from 3.8% and the highest since September 2023, matching economists' expectations. Core inflation held at 2.5%, while services inflation edged up to 3.3%.

The ECB wage tracker offered a distinct, more favorable prospective observation. It projected annual pay growth of 2.8% in both Q1 and Q2 2027, slowing to 2.4% in Q3. These contracted-pay indications suggested less wage pressure ahead even as current energy costs lifted headline inflation. Bloomberg Economics' David Powell judged underlying pass-through still limited and expected the hiking cycle to end after a final December increase.

Klaas Knot, whose nomination for the ECB presidency was confirmed by the Netherlands on Wednesday, emphasized the opposing risk. He expected core inflation to pick up through second-round effects in goods and services and argued for a somewhat hawkish stance against repeated supply shocks. Knot, the former Dutch central-bank chief rather than a current national governor, stressed the long policy lag: rates set now would become effective only after roughly 18 months to two years. His warning concerned prospective propagation, while the wage tracker pointed to slower negotiated pay.

Sweden acted immediately. The Riksbank unanimously raised its policy rate to 2% from 1.75%, its first increase since 2023, and said further tightening next year was likely if the inflation and activity outlook held. It issued no new forecast or rate path at the interim meeting. Governor Erik Thedéen said the existing path implied just under two additional increases over the coming year, without committing to individual meetings.

Nordea interpreted the guidance as making December unlikely and expects another move in February. Nomura expects quarter-point increases in February and May, potentially each delayed by a month. Bloomberg Economics forecasts one further increase to 2.25% in early 2027, with risks toward more tightening. Sweden's stronger growth has become part of that judgment: the finance ministry recently raised its 2026 growth estimate to 3%, even though hydroelectricity, nuclear generation and fuel-tax reductions had cushioned the energy shock.

Poland instead held at 3.75% for an eighth month while substantially raising its 2027 inflation projection. The new range was 3.1%-5.3%, against 1.5%-4% in July. October inflation had slowed to 3.5% from 4.1% after the government restored fuel-price caps. Bank Pekao economists said the council wanted to see whether those caps would be extended and whether second-round pressure appeared in realized data.

Polish two-year local yields fell 11 basis points to 4.83% and the zloty gained 0.4% against the euro. ING's Rafal Benecki still expected 50 basis points of increases in Q1 2027, but said continued energy declines would diminish the need. Separately, Tusk's approval of central-bank management-board appointments ended an operational dispute. It did not settle the parliamentary effort to put Governor Adam Glapinski before a tribunal over alleged misconduct, which he denies. The appointments and potential suspension involve different institutional decisions.

Britain's new services survey and research gave the expected Bank of England increase a firmer demand backdrop. S&P Global Services PMI rose to 52.8 from 52.1, the strongest activity reading since February. New orders recovered, staffing increased after an extended period of reductions, and input-price inflation reached a five-month high. IT and professional services benefited from AI-related business investment, while consumer-facing companies continued to report weaker demand.

Bloomberg Economics' Simon Lloyd and Dan Hanson challenged the BOE's assessment that policy was already restrictive. Their estimate of excess demand had stayed within a narrow range since Q4 2023 and stood at minus 0.2% of potential output in Q2 2026. They argued the economy was closer to its noninflationary capacity than the BOE assumed and that rates were broadly neutral for spending. Their forecast calls for increases this Thursday and in February; the research is a competing estimate of the economy's condition, not an official reassessment by the central bank.

Australia's September household-spending release also revealed demand resilience with an important price-volume distinction. Spending rose 0.6% monthly after a 0.1% decline, exceeding the 0.2% expectation, and was 6.8% higher annually at about A$82.6 billion. Non-discretionary expenditure increased 1.2%, and nominal spending rose across all states and territories. Fuel spending jumped 5.4%, partly reflecting higher oil prices and the end of excise relief, but experimental fuel volumes fell 2.2%. Across the quarter, real household spending increased 0.7%, its fourth consecutive gain.

China's RatingDog services PMI weakened to 50.8 from 51.6, below a 51.7 forecast and the lowest since July. Export orders expanded for a sixth month and hiring continued, but selling prices declined for a second month while input costs rose at their fastest pace in five months. The survey pointed to pressure on margins and confidence rather than the same domestic pricing strength reported in Britain.

Brazil's central bank unanimously held the Selic at 13.75%, ending five consecutive cuts, as 26 of 31 surveyed economists expected. Its statement paired higher inflation expectations and increased uncertainty with a more pronounced economic slowdown. The decision was scheduled after 6:30 p.m. Brasília time, late in the U.S. trading day, and is a separate policy development rather than an explanation for the earlier Treasury rally. The new fact was the pause itself and the board's assessment, after the election-driven reassessment of future rates already reported earlier in the week.

Chile's newly published October 27 minutes showed that a quarter-point increase had received serious consideration before policymakers held at 4.5%. Some members saw a solid basis for tightening against a larger cost shock, while others stressed the possibility of persistently weak demand. The minutes exposed a live policy alternative within the board, rather than announcing a new increase.

## Borrowing Authorizations and Creditor Rights Advance

U.S. voters approved at least $67 billion of state and local bond authorizations in preliminary tallies, creating a prospective financing pipeline rather than immediate issuance. California accounted for two major measures: $25 billion of revenue bonds for home-buying assistance and $11.25 billion of general-obligation debt for affordable housing. Dearborn Public Schools in Michigan secured approval for $1.5 billion of building work.

The approvals came from at least $84 billion proposed nationwide, exceeding approximately $81 billion debated in 2024. Not all borrowers obtained authority: Texas voters rejected a $1.6 billion Cypress-Fairbanks school package and a $952 million Irving school package. Franklin Templeton's Jennifer Johnston linked some defeats to resistance to higher taxes, even where population growth increases infrastructure needs. The election enlarged the borrowing pipeline while leaving some rapidly growing communities without their proposed financing.

Corporate credit faced a different question of investor rights. Electronic Arts sued bond trustee US Bank on Tuesday, seeking a declaration that it was not in default following its leveraged buyout. Creditors purportedly holding more than $1.4 billion of notes argue the company failed to make a required change-of-control payment. EA says an investment-grade Egan-Jones rating allows it to use defeasance, supporting future payments with Treasury collateral and avoiding the obligation.

The disputed economics are substantial. EA's February offer would have paid roughly 92 cents for its 1.85% notes due in 2031 and 74 cents for its 2.95% notes due in 2051, compared with the typical 101-cent change-of-control payment. Bloomberg previously estimated roughly $250 million of savings if EA's strategy succeeded. EA now says creditor remedies could trigger cross-default provisions in approximately $18 billion of parent-company debt. Those are the company's claims about possible consequences of the dispute; the court has been asked to determine its default status.

Acquisition financing continued to approach the market. JPMorgan and Bank of America are preparing to pre-market about $2.4 billion of cross-border loans for CVC's purchase of IFF's food-ingredients business. JPMorgan leads the euro portion and Bank of America the dollar tranche, which could be about $1.5 billion. Broader syndication is expected in coming weeks. The acquisition values the operations at $4.3 billion, with IFF retaining 10%; the loans remain a proposed distribution rather than completed investor funding.

In India, newly reported household-debt comparisons exposed a constraint beneath consumption growth. Central-bank figures put household borrowing growth at 36% in the year through March and consumer debt at a record 46% of GDP. Centre for Social and Economic Progress figures showed borrowing growing roughly four times as fast as disposable income in 2025-2026. CLSA estimated debt service at about 13% of household income in the year through March 2025, against 10%-11% through much of the preceding decade.

The article reported limited evidence of widespread repayment stress and bank bad-loan ratios near multidecade lows. Nevertheless, Bajaj Finance and Piramal Finance had identified distressed borrowers using gold loans to support credit facilities already in default elsewhere. That observation concerns those borrowers, not all Indian consumers. Gold-backed borrowing rose nearly 45% in the year through March, while lenders have also shifted personal credit toward higher-income borrowers. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman defended the durability of consumption, leaving the pace of borrowing and repayment burdens central to the disagreement.

Kenya received a conditional assessment of how governance could improve sovereign financing. New World Bank modeling estimated that moderate anticorruption reform could raise GDP by 8.7% relative to a no-reform scenario by 2035, or 22.3% under stronger measures. It estimated a debt-to-GDP ratio as much as 18% lower relative to the status quo, not an 18-percentage-point debt reduction already achieved. Matching corruption-perception scores in Ivory Coast, Ghana or Senegal could reduce external borrowing costs by 50-100 basis points, saving $50 million-$100 million annually, the bank said.

Kenya is also seeking a $1 billion debt swap to support food programs. The proposed use of refinancing savings illustrates a shift in some developing-country debt conversions from conservation toward immediate affordability and education needs. Nuveen's Stephen Liberatore expects several publicly offered conversions next year. Separately, the World Bank's Paschal Donohoe advocated greater municipal issuance across sub-Saharan Africa, conditional on cities having the leadership and tax-raising capacity to service their own debt. These initiatives describe potential financing channels, not completed relief or an announced wave of new city bonds.

## Forward Market Significance

Thursday's U.S. jobless claims and Q3 productivity releases arrive at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. Claims consensus is 196,000 after 194,000, while productivity is expected to rise 2.5% after 1.4%. They will add evidence on dismissals and output efficiency to Wednesday's combination of above-consensus private hiring, slower services orders and persistent input costs. Beth Hammack and Tom Barkin are scheduled to speak Thursday, followed by Lorie Logan that evening, providing opportunities to assess the policy implications of the week's data and energy repricing.

Friday's October employment report remains the larger labor-market event. Consensus calls for 65,000 payroll growth after 29,000, with headline U-3 unemployment unchanged at 4.2%. Average hourly earnings are expected to increase 0.3% monthly and 2.9% annually. The hiring and wage combination will matter to a market that still assigns a high likelihood to December tightening. November's preliminary Michigan sentiment index follows, with consensus at 48, while John Williams, Alberto Musalem and Michelle Bowman also have scheduled appearances Friday.

The Bank of England's Thursday decision will show how officials interpret stronger business services alongside weaker household-facing demand. A quarter-point increase to 4% is widely expected. The substantive uncertainty is how much further tightening officials judge necessary, especially as Bloomberg Economics challenges the assumption that the existing rate already restrains spending. ECB presidential nominations close Friday, after the Netherlands confirmed Knot; finance ministers will take stock November 9 without a decision yet foreseen.

Treasury will auction $58 billion of three-year notes November 9, $42 billion of 10-year notes November 10 and $25 billion of 30-year bonds November 12. The $125 billion refunding is unchanged for an 11th consecutive round. Actual demand at those sales will follow an announcement that left auction sizes intact while moving dealer forecasts farther into the future. The debt-limit negotiations present a longer-dated and distinct risk: reaching the legal ceiling and exhausting cash after extraordinary measures are separate stages, with any maturity-specific bill disruption dependent on the eventual financing deadline.

For AI credit, the pending policy question is how incoming governors translate campaign promises into permitting decisions, and how existing approvals and customer contracts are treated. CoreWeave's statement about unchanged commitments and the market's concern over development delays will meet project-specific decisions rather than a single nationwide rule. Meta's record euro order book also leaves the cost of subsequent funding important: access remained strong, but the price paid differed markedly from peers.

Energy diplomacy retains independent importance. Trump said the U.S. had no immediate plans to escalate the Iran conflict, while French Finance Minister Roland Lescure cautioned that foreign-policy authority remains with the president despite the election. Iran and the U.S. were reviewing mediator proposals amid continuing disagreement over the response. Whether that process sustains the fall in crude will shape the persistence of Wednesday's inflation-compensation decline; the election result alone does not settle the negotiations or restore unrestricted energy transport.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally as Democratic control of Congress and plunging oil ease fiscal and inflation risks
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied after Democrats won both chambers of Congress, limiting prospects for further fiscal expansion, while a sharp oil decline eased inflation risk. The 10-year yield fell 7.42 basis points to 4.8879%: inflation compensation dropped 5.94 basis points to 2.2485%, while the real yield declined 1.48 basis points to 2.6394%. Intermediate maturities led the advance, and the 2- to 10-year spread narrowed 2.42 basis points to 30.7 basis points. Brent fell 8.66% to $94.63 a barrel.

Treasury kept auction sizes unchanged despite revised guidance, leading dealers to postpone or abandon forecasts for long-bond supply cuts. Softer services surveys still showed expansion, ADP hiring beat expectations, and services input costs remained elevated. Expectations of December Fed tightening were little changed.

Proposed data-center restrictions divided credit markets. CoreWeave bonds reached new lows on development-delay concerns, although the company said existing commitments were not expected to be affected. Meta's credit protection became cheaper as investors anticipated less future borrowing, yet its debut euro sale still raised €9 billion against a record €53 billion order book at higher premiums than peers. Broad U.S. high-yield spreads tightened clearly as equities recovered. Whether energy diplomacy sustains cheaper crude remains important to the inflation-led bond rally.
